title: Authoring-friendly JSON schema profiles with graded diagnostics and autofix suggestions
creator: Jonah Park
description: Enable a practical authoring and runtime validation surface for tool/function call JSON schemas that produces graded diagnostic codes and human-friendly autofix suggestions. This ticket scopes a canonical profile set for schema authoring (editor-time) and a deterministic mapping from runtime validation failures to graded diagnostic messages and suggested remediation steps for SDKs and the Console. Goal: reduce ambiguous error messages, shorten developer feedback loop, and make migration of legacy tool shapes easier via safe autofix hints.
proposals: Define three authoring profiles: strict (for public, enforced contracts), advisory (lint-like warnings), and permissive (compatibility-first). Each profile maps to a runtime validation policy and a suggested autofix policy.
Introduce a compact diagnostic code namespace (TSK_xxx for tooling) with severity levels (INFO/WARN/ERROR) and machine-readable remediation hints (short label + patch snippet).
Implement a small 'autofix manifest' format that expresses single-step JSON transforms (rename, move, default-insert, type-coerce) that editors and the runtime can apply or present as suggestions.
Expose a validation endpoint in the SDK and Console that returns the canonical diagnostic list plus recommended autofix patches and an estimated safety score for each patch.
Backwards-compat shim: runtime can accept legacy field aliases and emit TSK_WARN codes with suggested rename transforms rather than hard failures.
acceptance_criteria: Spec doc exists defining the three profiles, diagnostic code taxonomy, remediation hint schema, and autofix manifest grammar (Confluence link in attachments).
Runtime validation library returns structured diagnostics (code, severity, path, human_message, remediation_hint) for all error classes in our taxonomy.
Console UI surfaces diagnostics with inline 'apply suggestion' action for simple autofix types (rename, insert default), and action flow is audited in the request log.
SDK validation call (validate_schema) implemented with stable JSON output consumed by editor LSP and Console, and included in unit tests covering edge cases in acceptance matrix.
Migration experiment: convert 10 sampled legacy tool manifests; validation emits WARN-level hints and 80% of suggested autofixes are applicable without manual edits in developer trial.

notes: Tradeoffs: strict profile reduces runtime ambiguity but increases breakage risk. Permissive profile improves compatibility but hides class of problems until runtime UX surfaces them.

Autofix safety: only include transforms with deterministic behavior (rename with single unambiguous mapping, default insertion for missing required primitives). Complex fixes will be surfaced as suggestions that open an authoring modal rather than one-click apply.
We should align diagnostic numbering with existing telemetry to avoid duplicate namespaces. Proposed prefix: TSK for tooling, followed by 3-digit code (e.g., TSK_101).
Security: ensure autofix apply flow requires the same auth scope as schema edits; do not auto-apply for tenant-shared schemas without explicit owner approval.

error_codes: TSK_100 ERROR invalid-type: field expected type string but got number — remediation: check caller schema, provide type-coerce autofix if safe (e.g., number->string) where explicit cast allowed.
TSK_101 WARN unexpected-property: field not present in schema — remediation: suggested rename aliases or mark as additionalProperties=true in permissive profile.
TSK_102 WARN missing-optional: optional field missing default — remediation: propose default insert or leave advisory.
TSK_200 INFO deprecation: using deprecated field name — remediation: hint with rename suggestion and include deprecation window in message.
TSK_300 ERROR ambiguous-rename: multiple candidate fields match rename heuristic — remediation: surface as action requiring manual resolution in Console.
TSK_400 WARN unsafe-autofix: transform exists but low confidence — remediation: surface in editor as suggestion, do not auto-apply.
TSK_500 ERROR schema-invalid: schema authoring errors (malformed JSON-schema subset) — remediation: link to authoring guide and example fixes.
telemetry_schema: diagnostic.path: string JSONPath to failing node
editor_integration_notes: Expose validate_schema endpoint used by LSP to display inline diagnostics and quick-fix code actions.
Quick-fix actions should include the autofix manifest patch and a preview of the patch to be applied in the editor before confirm.
LSP should request validation with explicit profile hint; default to advisory for unsaved drafts to reduce noisy errors.
Provide a 'preview-only' flag in the SDK so editors can show potential changes without persisting them.
